vulnerability_name: Missing HTTP Security Headers and Verbose Internal Debug Error Exposure
severity_justification: Missing defense-in-depth headers increases susceptibility to Clickjacking (UI redressing) and MIME-type sniffing. Verbose stack traces leak server paths, dependency versions, and internal implementation details to attackers.
root_cause: The application ran with Flask debug mode enabled by default and lacked explicit HTTP response header hardening middleware.
safe_reproduction_steps: 1. Start the application in vulnerable mode (SECURESHOP_MODE=vulnerable).
2. Inspect HTTP response headers using curl or browser DevTools: curl -I http://127.0.0.1:5000/
expected_vulnerable_behavior: Headers X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options are absent. Error endpoint displays full Python traceback and environment variables.
observed_evidence: HTTP response shows 'Server: Werkzeug/Debug-Unshielded'. No X-Frame-Options or CSP headers present. Unhandled exception displays complete code traceback revealing filesystem paths.
potential_impact: Clickjacking attacks embedding the application in malicious iframes; information disclosure aiding targeted exploit development.
remediation: Implemented `apply_security_headers` middleware in `secureshop.services.security_middleware` setting X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and strict Content-Security-Policy. Enforced custom sanitized 500 error handler in `secureshop/__init__.py`.
retest_result: PASS. All 5 recommended security headers are present. 500 server error displays a generic, friendly error message with zero stack trace leakage.
